title: Screenshot carousel's mandatory scroll-snap traps vertical scroll, making the bottom ~40% of the page unreachable
detail: LandingClient.tsx:1673 sets scrollSnapType:'x mandatory' on a viewport-wide overflow-x:auto flex row (1646-1718) inside the nested #landing-scroll container. In Chromium, vertical wheel/trackpad gestures over a mandatory-snap horizontal scroller are re-targeted to the snap axis; because the strip spans full viewport width, the pointer is almost always over it and vertical scrolling stalls — live testing (2026-07-16) confirmed even End/PageUp cannot escape. globals.css:69-72 (.mp-scroll overscroll-behavior:contain) removes the scroll-chaining fallback on touch; horizontal overscroll also chains into Android back/forward gestures (no overscrollBehaviorX:contain). Net effect: comparison table, audience, testimonials, 12-question FAQ (also emitted as JSON-LD), app-store badges, final CTA, and footer are unreachable. The carousel has zero keyboard/AT affordances (no tabIndex, no prev/next, no dots, no aria-roledescription) — hard WCAG 2.1.1/2.4.3 failure — and its only affordance is a rgba(198,107,61,0.4) scrollbar thumb at ~1.9:1 contrast (styles 824-837). Staging code shows a plain overflow div, suggesting deployed bundle drift — the exact prod-drift root cause documented 2026-07-12.
recommendation: Priority zero: first verify prod runs current code (deploy drift has bitten this page before). Then remove 'x mandatory' (use 'x proximity' or none) — never convert vertical wheel/key input into horizontal movement. Best: static grid on desktop, swipe strip only on touch. If any carousel survives: visible 44px prev/next buttons calling scrollBy(), dots, tabIndex=0 with arrow keys, aria-roledescription='carousel', overscroll-behavior-x:contain, full-opacity thumb. Re-test hero-to-footer as one uninterrupted scroll via wheel, keyboard (End/PageDown/Space), and touch — this single fix unlocks four already-built sections of proof and objection handling.

title: Entire page scrolls inside a custom 100dvh div, structurally breaking keyboard scrolling, scroll restoration, and iOS viewport behavior
detail: The page root is <div id='landing-scroll'> with height:100dvh, overflowY:auto (LandingClient.tsx:610-621), so the document never scrolls. Keyboard scroll keys target the focused element's nearest scrollable ancestor, falling back to document.scrollingElement — which has no overflow — so End/PageUp/Space are no-ops until the user clicks inside the div, and once focus lands in the carousel, End/Home scroll it horizontally (keyboard scrolling does not chain to ancestors). It also breaks browser scroll restoration on back-navigation, iOS tap-status-bar scroll-to-top, and — because the body never scrolls — iOS Safari's URL bar never collapses, so the hero's minHeight:100vh (1079) permanently exceeds the visible viewport, clipping the scroll hint and pushing CTAs to the bottom edge on 667-812px phones.
recommendation: Let the document scroll: drop the fixed-height inner scroller, use normal body flow (nav is already position:fixed; the scroll listener at 575-581 can read window.scrollY). Native document scroll gives keyboard keys, scrollbar, scroll restoration, find-in-page, and fragment links for free — Linear/Stripe/Apple never use custom scrollers on marketing pages. Use minHeight:100svh for the hero. If the scroller must stay, add tabIndex + programmatic focus on mount and audit that no nested scrollable steals End/Home.

title: "End-to-End Encrypted" claim is factually false — hero chip, /security SEO metadata, blog, all 5 locales
detail: Provably untrue: the only crypto in the repo is HMAC webhook verification (api/webhooks/whatsapp/route.ts:111-119) — no libsodium/tweetnacl/WebCrypto content encryption anywhere; all uploads send plaintext to Supabase Storage; the server demonstrably reads content (ai-label/route.ts:90-108 sends user photos to a third-party AI provider — definitionally incompatible with E2EE; AI interviews, WhatsApp ingestion, sharing, OG images all require server plaintext); busts/profile-photos are served via getPublicUrl. The product's own /security page correctly claims only TLS 1.2+ in transit and AES-256 at rest (en.json:3592-3598), so the contradiction is one click away. The false chip ships in all 5 locales (landing.trustBadges.encrypted, line 1330 each, rendered LandingClient.tsx:1256); worse, src/app/security/layout.tsx lines 5/8/25 (description, openGraph, twitter) also promise "end-to-end encryption" — the SERP snippet promises E2EE and the landed page disproves it. The site's own blog (src/lib/blog/posts/en.ts:1369) even coaches readers to ask vendors about E2EE. For a GDPR-positioned EU heritage app targeting 60+ users this is UCPD misleading-practice exposure and a one-tweet reputation risk, trivially falsifiable by a journalist, Apple reviewer, or the security-literate gift-giving adult child.
section: Hero trust chips (LandingClient.tsx:1256; all 5 locale files line 1330) + src/app/security/layout.tsx:5,8,25 + blog
recommendation: Replace trustBadges.encrypted in all 5 locales — EN "Encrypted at Rest & in Transit", NL "Versleuteld bij opslag & verzending", DE "Verschlüsselt bei Speicherung & Übertragung", ES "Cifrado en reposo y en tránsito", FR "Chiffré au repos et en transit". Do not soften to "Fully Encrypted" (re-implies E2EE). Fix all three security/layout.tsx descriptions to "AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS in transit, and GDPR compliance". Sweep every file containing the string (messages/*.json, blog en.ts/nl.ts, security/layout.tsx). Add a pre-deploy grep gate for "end-to-end|E2EE|bank-grade" across src/messages and src/app. Make every security chip link to /security — the honest page is the strongest proof.

title: Testimonials appear fabricated (per-se banned under EU law post-Omnibus) and "Join thousands" is unverifiable — on landing, /pricing, and in-app
detail: en.json:1273-1289 contains four invented-looking quotes with full names and ages ("Margaret van den Berg, 72", "Robert Hendriks, 65", "Elisabeth Janssen, 44" with a quasi-therapeutic dementia claim, "Karel de Vries, 58" claiming "15,000 images sorted in under an hour"), rendered with hardcoded 5-star SVGs and CSS-gradient initial avatars (LandingClient.tsx:463-467, ~2030) — each mapping 1:1 to a marketing pillar, with no photos, city, or verifiability. /pricing already ships "Maria S." and "Thomas K." (en.json:1899-1904); in-app interview.socialProof (en.json:4436) says "Join thousands preserving life stories" while the product is beta-stage. Since the Omnibus Directive (2019/2161), fake consumer reviews are a per-se banned commercial practice in every EU member state (fines up to 4% of turnover in the launch locales). Quote2 also claims recording a video message — a capability that does not exist. Currently unreachable only because of the scroll trap; fixing the carousel will surface them. One discovered fake grief quote is fatal for a brand whose entire promise is truthful preservation of real lives.
recommendation: Verify each quote maps to a real, consenting user or remove all of them (landing + /pricing + all 5 locales) before the redesign ships; reword socialProof to a number-free claim. Replace with real consented quotes — MP has real users to ask (Android v1.0.1 testers, Guillaume, featured_palaces owners): first name + last initial minimum, real age, written consent, no invented performance numbers, no price mentions (iOS seal). If none are ready, cut the section — an absent section is invisible; a fake one is fatal. Keep the dementia/adult-child story ANGLE as an explicitly labeled scenario, not a fake person. Copy rule: no user counts, star ratings, or review counts until queried from the DB and above a vanity floor.

title: Apple 3.1.1 seal has live holes on the landing page: exit-intent modal, un-gated "Free / Forever Plan" stat, credit-card body copy, VoiceOver labels, and a fragile dash-stripping mechanism
detail: After six rejections on builds 46-53, each hole is a live re-rejection vector: (1) exit-intent CTA renders "Create Your Palace — Free" without iosCta() (LandingClient.tsx:2713) and the guard at 592-605 only skips isMobile (≤767px) — an iPad in the iOS app with trackpad/Pencil hover can fire mouseleave and show the exact qualifier Apple flagged. (2) The trust bar renders TRUST_STATS unconditionally (1332-1356), so iOS still shows "Free / Forever Plan" — "Plan" implies other paid plans, the wording pattern Apple cited 2026-07-09. (3) midCta "Your palace is free. No credit card, no catch." (en.json:1191 → line 1556) and cta.description "Free forever. No credit card..." (en.json:1291 → 2269) render un-gated; mentioning credit cards implies purchasable content. (4) aria-labels "Create your palace for free" (en.json:1316-1318, applied 1182/2274) are never stripped — VoiceOver announces "free" on sealed buttons, also a WCAG 2.5.3 divergence. (5) iosCta() (545-548) is runtime string surgery splitting on em/en dashes — any copy edit with a hyphen or qualifier-first ordering silently re-leaks with no build signal; nl.json:1369 ("Maak je Palace — Gratis", untranslated) proves keys drift independently.
section: Exit-intent (LandingClient.tsx:592-605, 2624-2717), trust bar (1332-1356), mid/final CTA (1556, 2269), a11y keys (en.json:1313-1319), iosCta (545-548)
recommendation: (1) Add `if (isIosApp) return;` to the exit-intent effect AND wrap its label in iosCta() for defense in depth. (2) Gate stat2 on isIosApp to a neutral pair ("Unlimited / Wings & Rooms"). (3) Add explicit *_ios message keys mirroring the existing faq a4_ios pattern: midCta.text_ios "Your palace is ready in minutes. No tech skills needed."; cta.description_ios equivalent — web keeps the credit-card reassurance. (4) Drop custom aria-labels or set them equal to visible labels with pricing words removed. (5) Retire dash-stripping in favor of price-free primary labels plus a CI grep failing on /free|gratis|kostenlos|gratuit|credit card/i in any key rendered on the iOS path. Sweep all 5 locales.

title: iOS Apple-3.1.1 seal is two-layered and depends on dynamic SSR — the redesign must preserve both layers verbatim
detail: Seal = (1) page.tsx server-seeds initialIosApp into LandingClient so SSR HTML has zero paid surfaces on iOS, and (2) middleware.ts:36 redirects native-iOS /pricing to /atrium. The first-paint seal works only because page.tsx calls cookies()/headers(), keeping the route dynamic. A redesign that adds force-static/ISR, moves the landing to static export, or does iOS detection client-only reintroduces sealed-HTML flashes — the exact failure mode behind prior 3.1.1 rejections (stale/static prod, 2026-07-12 audit).
recommendation: Carry the initialIosApp prop plumbing and conditional rendering of paid CTAs/pricing links through the new component tree verbatim; never make the landing route static or client-detect-only. Post-deploy, verify with curl -A MemoryPalace-iOS (and mp_platform=ios cookie) that SSR HTML contains no pricing/"— Free" strings. Any new pricing block, gift flow, or plan badge added during the redesign must sit behind the same gate.

title: Below-hero content is SSR'd as empty placeholders (LazySection), producing hero-only indexed HTML, JSON-LD content mismatch, blank beige voids, and scroll-time layout shift
detail: All 8 sections after the hero are wrapped in LazySection (LandingClient.tsx:78-85), which SSRs an empty placeholder div (12-30rem minHeight vs real 1500-2500px sections) and mounts children only on IntersectionObserver: (1) none of the features/how-it-works/comparison/testimonials/FAQ text exists in served HTML — Google (whose tall-viewport render never scrolls the nested container), Bing, and AI-search crawlers index an essentially hero-only page, and the FAQPage JSON-LD (line 646) describes Q&A text absent from the DOM, a structured-data mismatch under Google's guidelines; (2) document height inflates repeatedly while scrolling — scrollbar jumps, End lands at a bottom that then moves, scrollIntoView('#how-it-works') (1201) lands at the wrong offset (no scroll-margin-top anywhere, fixed nav overlaps anchors); (3) ScrollFadeIn (88-102) holds content at opacity:0 until 10% in-viewport then staggers per-card (delay 0.05+i*0.07, line 1412), so whole viewports show nothing but background — the observed 'huge dead whitespace' is largely this choreography, and if JS fails the walkthrough video and carousel are permanently invisible. The 'lazy' machinery saves nothing: the content is text and inline SVG.
recommendation: Remove LazySection: always render section children on the server (the text IS the SEO asset) and use CSS content-visibility:auto + contain-intrinsic-size for paint savings with zero layout shift. Put ids on real <section> elements with scroll-margin-top:5rem. Make ScrollFadeIn start visible by default or use a generous positive rootMargin (~200-300px lead) so elements are opaque before entering view; cap at ~300ms, no per-item stagger, honor prefers-reduced-motion, hidden-state as a post-hydration class so no-JS users see content. Rule: no pixel blank longer than 150ms after entering the viewport; CLS during scroll = 0.

title: All 5 full locale JSONs (~1.5 MB raw, ~348 KB gzip) are statically bundled into the landing client chunk
detail: LandingClient.tsx:11-19 statically imports en/nl/de/es/fr.json (265-322 KB each — the ENTIRE app's ~11k keys per locale, not just `landing`) into a landingMessages map. Verified in the build: four chunks of 84-89 KB gzip each are literally the locale files (confirmed by grepping 'souvenirs'/'recuerdos'/'Erinnerungen'/'herinneringen' in .next/static/chunks). An English visitor downloads and parses four languages they will never see — ~7 s extra on 3G plus a large main-thread JSON parse on an older iPad. Ironically src/lib/hooks/useTranslation.ts already lazy-loads these exact files via dynamic import(); the static imports defeat that system.
recommendation: Delete the static message imports and rely on useTranslation's existing dynamic loading (en.json is already the sync fallback). Better: extract a landing-only namespace per locale (~5-10 KB) and have the server wrapper (page.tsx) read the locale and pass only that slice as props, so zero translation JSON ships in the client bundle.

title: ~580 KB gzip of client JS for a static marketing page — and the primary CTA is dead until hydration
detail: The whole 2,719-line page is one 'use client' component; its client-module chunks sum to 579,737 bytes gzipped (measured via page_client-reference-manifest.js), before main files, PostHog, and the service worker. Everything below the hero is static text/SVG needing no JS, yet it all hydrates. Worse, the hero "Create Your Palace — Free" CTA is a <button onClick> (~line 1179), not a link — on a 3G/older-iPad first visit the most important element silently does nothing for the seconds until React hydrates; a 65-year-old taps once, nothing happens, and concludes the site is broken. (Verified positive: three.js is NOT in the bundle.)
recommendation: Make both hero CTAs real <a href> anchors that work pre-hydration (keep analytics as non-blocking click handlers). Split the page: server components for stats, features, how-it-works, comparison, FAQ; small client islands only for the carousel, FAQ accordion, and language switcher. Target <100 KB gzip client JS — Linear, Stripe, and Arc landing pages work with JS disabled.

title: Hero first paint is a brown void: video triple-dimmed to ~10-15% luminance, no poster, low-bitrate single MP4, and LCP text animating from opacity 0
detail: The Tuscan-villa footage is stacked under three darkening layers: <video> at opacity:0.3 with filter saturate(0.6) brightness(0.85) (HeroVideo, LandingClient.tsx:149-150), solid charcoal section background (1088), and a rgba(42,34,24, 0.65→0.45→0.7) gradient scrim (1101) — users literally cannot see the villa, and the per-frame CSS filter is continuous GPU compositing cost on the largest element. No poster and preload='metadata' overridden by autoplay means first paint is a blank dark-brown box while 2.06 MB downloads (all viewports incl. cellular); the source is only 1280x732 @ ~915 kbps H.264 upscaled to full viewport (banding in dark gradients), with no WebM/AV1 and no mobile encode — while better masters (hero-bg-original.mp4/hero-ob.mp4, 1792x1024) sit unused in public/video/. The scrim dips to 0.45 exactly behind the text so contrast fluctuates frame-by-frame (hence the double text-shadow crutch at 1137), and the scrim base rgba(42,34,24) mismatches the #1F1B1A section, producing a two-tone seam pre-load. Compounding it, the h1 animates 'fadeUp 0.7s ease 0.1s both' from opacity:0 with staggers to +0.5s (1115-1249) — Chrome cannot record LCP for unpainted text, ~0.8 s of LCP penalty by design, and on slow devices the first seconds are a dark empty screen. Emotionally, the gloom reads funereal for a persona whose parent may be dying.
section: Section 1 — HeroVideo (LandingClient.tsx:105-157), scrim (1096-1104), text animation (1115-1249), public/video/
recommendation: Re-encode from hero-bg-original.mp4: 1080p H.264 ~1.5-3 Mbps + AV1/WebM source with the warm golden-hour grade baked in (delete the CSS filter); run at ~0.6-0.7 opacity with ONE bottom/behind-text scrim (~0.65 uniform behind the headline block, derived from C.charcoal). Add poster='/video/hero-poster.jpg' (~40-80 KB graded frame) with <link rel='preload' as='image' fetchpriority='high'>. On mobile and saveData/2g-3g connections skip video and ship the still. Never animate the LCP candidate from opacity 0 — render the headline visible immediately, reserve entrances for secondary elements. Test: paused at second zero, the frame must answer 'what is this?' and make you feel something.

title: Zero product visual in the first viewport, and the 3D product is never shown passively anywhere — a walkable 3D palace sold with text alone
detail: The hero is 100vh of centered typography; the product's entire differentiation — a walkable 3D palace — first appears at section 6 as 'Guillaume's Palace': a 900px-max, click-to-play <video controls preload=metadata> (LandingClient.tsx:1607-1636) most visitors will only ever see as a poster. The eye travels dimmed abstract video → text stats → 12 text cards → 3 text steps → text micro-CTA before any real product visual, and the single genuine interior demonstration requires an active click after ~5 sections of scrolling. In the first 5 seconds a visitor cannot answer 'what does this look like?'. Category-defining visual products (Linear, Arc, Figma, Framer) always put the product in frame one and autoplay short muted loops inline, reserving long video for a modal. An animated LandingPalacePreview component exists unused, and a real walkable demo palace sits behind the unexposed /explore guest-visit flow.
recommendation: Put a bright, legible 3D palace interior in the first viewport: split hero (headline + high-quality render) or a 10-15 s muted autoplaying interior flyover loop (dolly through the entrance hall past hung photos) as the hero background or directly under it — no click required. Keep the full narrated walkthrough as click-to-play in a lightbox. Then feature cards can reference what the visitor just saw. The 5-second test: 'oh — my photos live inside a beautiful 3D house I can walk through.'

title: Systemic WCAG AA contrast and type-size failures: walnut body text, terracotta labels/stat numbers, CTA gradient, and 62 sub-1rem sizes — for a 60+ audience
detail: C.walnut #8B7355 is the de-facto muted ink and fails 4.5:1 everywhere: 12 feature descriptions at 15px (featureDesc 2815-2819, ~3.9-4.3:1), FAQ answers (217), group subtitles (1392, 3.8:1), how-it-works steps on warmStone (1522, 3.3:1), stats labels at 13px (1349), nav links (2730), exit-modal body (2689). sectionLabel terracotta #C66B3D at 13px is ~3.2:1 on linen / 2.8:1 on warmStone and can never pass on either. The stats bar — the strip making GDPR/encryption claims — fails on BOTH layers (terracotta numbers 2.8:1, below even the 3:1 large-text threshold). Every primary CTA is white 1rem/600 text on a terracotta→walnut gradient: 3.6:1 at the start, 4.3:1 at the end — the most important button fails AA for its own label. Grep shows 62 fontSize declarations under 1rem, including 11px scroll hints, 12px trust chips (the key senior reassurance is the least readable text), and 14px comparison cells. The file already defines an audited token — MUTED_ON_LIGHT #716A5E, line 264, commented '~4.6:1' — used in exactly one section. NIA/NN-g senior guidance: 16px floor, prefer 18px; contrast sensitivity declines ~1%/year after 40. This is the primary persona failing to read the value proposition.
section: Systemic — feature cards, stats bar (1316-1356), eyebrows, CTAs (2747-2776), nav, chips (LandingClient.tsx throughout)
recommendation: One sweep: replace every text use of C.walnut with MUTED_ON_LIGHT or darker (verify per background; ~#5E574C on warmStone), mark walnut as non-text ink in theme.ts. Eyebrows: C.rustDeep #9A4F2A on light (5.1:1), C.gold on dark (8.1:1, already correct once at 1657); floor uppercase labels at 0.75rem, tokenize tracking in em not px. CTAs: darken to rustDeep→rustDarker (#9A4F2A→#6B3318 — 5.7:1/8.9:1, and reads more 'Tuscan fresco' than orange-tan), keep terracotta as hover glow. Stats: rustDeep or charcoal numbers, ≥4.5:1 labels. Raise the floor to 1rem for all functional text, 1.125rem for body/feature copy; audit all 62 sub-1rem declarations. Verify at 200% zoom (WCAG 1.4.4).

title: Twelve identical text-only cards flatten the differentiators into a beige wall: forced 4/4/4 symmetry, ~25-30 CPL copy, dead-end divs, and meaningless icon tiles on mobile
detail:
'Twelve ways your memories stay vivid' (en.json:1139) delivers a 3x4 grid of visually identical white cards (featureCard 2799-2805: 1.12:1 vs linen, 48px thin-line icons, ~450 words of sub-AA 15px copy at ~25-30 characters per line in ~200-210px card interiors). The category-defining 3D palace is card #5, weighted identically to commodity 'Upload Photos & Videos — drag, drop, done' (literally Google Photos' core feature); the emotionally devastating features (Time Capsules, AI Interviews' 'the questions your grandchildren would ask') are flattened to the same rank. The Capture/Enrich/Share taxonomy demanded 4/4/4 parallelism, so weak cards pad slots — clearest case 'Explore & Connect' (en.json:1174), whose public-publishing/follower framing is off-brief for privacy-motivated Keepers and plants 'wait, is my palace public?' one viewport below the GDPR chips. Every card is a static div (1413-1423) — nothing clickable, no next action. On <480px, descriptions are dropped entirely ({!isSmall &&

}, line 1422), leaving twelve non-tappable icon+title tiles ('Legacy Planning') that carry no meaning — precisely on the device where gift-giving adult children first encounter the product. Zero product imagery for inherently visual features. Per persona, four features carry ~80% of persuasion.
section: Section 3 — features grid (LandingClient.tsx:1360-1430, FEATURE_GROUPS 424-455, styles 2799-2819; en.json:1139-1174)
recommendation: Two-tier restructure: Tier 1 — 4 flagship features (3D Palace, AI Interviews, WhatsApp Capture, Co-Creation/Time Capsules) as large alternating image+text bands with real product assets (flyover loop, transcript animation, phone frame with a voice note landing in a room), each with one bold 6-10-word benefit headline + one sentence at ≥1.0625rem and an inline action ('Watch the flyover', 'See a shared palace'). Tier 2 — the rest collapse to one compact icon-chip strip linking to /features. Cut 'Explore & Connect' from the landing. Kill the count from the headline; lead with the outcome. On mobile, 4-6 full-width curated cards with a one-line desc + screenshot and a 'See all features' disclosure. Total section copy down ~65%. Move the block to after the product demonstration; keep the iOS seal (no pricing-adjacent CTAs).

title: A desktop 3D product is showcased almost entirely via 15rem-wide phone-frame App Store screenshots with baked-in captions — under the page's boldest claim
detail: The section declaring 'THIS IS NOT A PHOTO ALBUM / This is a palace' (first line demoted to a small gold eyebrow, LandingClient.tsx:1657-1662) pays it off with 8 portrait store screenshots at ~240px wide on desktop (1681-1714): repurposed App Store assets with marketing captions baked into the bitmaps (unlocalizable, invisible to screen readers), alt text 'The Memory Palace app — screen N' (1702 — WCAG 1.1.1 failure even though the filenames prove descriptive text exists), raw with no width/height (CLS risk), wrong aspect and device frame, inside the darkest section, inside the broken carousel. There are zero large desktop-viewport renders anywhere on the page — visually saying 'small mobile app', contradicting 'cinematic'. Supporting-asset audit: all existing 3D captures include UI chrome, the largest desktop shots are 1200x750 webp or orphaned PNGs, interiors read low-poly, the best emotional clip (hero-ob.mp4 — a person touching framed photos in a sunlit arcade) is used only in OnboardingWizard, and no imagery shows memories INSIDE the palace (photos hung on a 3D wall).
recommendation: Shoot dedicated landing renders: fresh 2x-retina UI-free captures of the best scenes (exterior dusk, entrance hall, a filled memory room with demo photos in frames) at 1100-1400px desktop aspect, presented frameless as alternating image/text bands with HTML captions (i18n) and real alt text. Stage a lived-in demo palace with licensed period family photos and shoot everything from it; add one 'from shoebox to palace' juxtaposition band — the signature shot no competitor can match. Set both headline lines at full scale and pay off with one full-bleed interior. Keep phone frames for a single explicit 'also on your phone' moment; feature hero-ob.mp4 in the hero or the 'not a photo album' section.

title: The only product film is completely silent — no audio stream, no captions, a single 12.4 MB rendition — while the hero sells 'voices'
detail: ffprobe confirms public/video/walkthrough.mp4 ('Guillaume's Palace', LandingClient.tsx:1622-1635) contains exactly one h264 stream: no audio at all, yet the player renders controls, so users get a volume button that does nothing. No <track> caption files exist despite 5 locales (WCAG 1.2.2 — acute for a 60+ audience where ~a third has hearing loss). The file is 12,455,086 bytes MP4-only with no resolution ladder — a 4G mobile user who taps play commits to 12 MB for a ~350px-wide video. The hero literally sells 'photos, voices, and stories' and the only product film is mute. (The poster-first, preload='metadata', tap-to-play pattern is already correct — keep it.)
recommendation: Produce one narrated 45-60 s cut: warm human voice-over ('This is Guillaume's palace…'), light ambient score, ending on the free CTA. Ship WebVTT captions for EN/NL/DE/ES/FR via <track kind='captions'> plus a short transcript. Encode a 720p ~3-4 MB rendition or move to Mux/Cloudflare Stream for adaptive bitrate. If narration can't ship immediately: score + captions and remove the misleading volume control. Present it as attributed proof: 'Guillaume's palace — a real member's home for three generations of memories.'

title: French landing copy is broken: ~28+ strings missing diacritics plus calques and faux-amis — reads as spam to any French visitor, including in FAQ JSON-LD
detail: src/messages/fr.json ships accent-stripped French in the most visible strings: hero 'Vos souvenirs meritent un palais' (méritent), CTA 'Creez votre palais — Gratuit', 'Decouvrez comment ca marche', trust chips 'Chiffre SSL', 'Heberge dans l'UE', 'Protege par le RGPD', plus FAQ answers a1/a2/a7 that are emitted as FAQPage JSON-LD — Google shows broken French in rich results. Other keys in the same file are correctly accented ('Fonctionnalités'), proving a machine-mangled batch, not encoding. Beyond accents: 'un palais 3D qui ressemble a un foyer' (calque reading as 'looks like a hearth'), 'Pas du stockage.' (ungrammatical), 'Huit parcours curates' (faux-ami). Accent-less calqued marketing copy is fatal for a trust-first heritage product aimed at 60+ users.
section: All FR sections — src/messages/fr.json (hero, trust bar, features, how-it-works, FAQ/JSON-LD)
recommendation: One native-French rewrite pass of the whole landing namespace: restore all diacritics and fix idiom ('un palais 3D où l'on se sent chez soi'; 'Ce n'est pas du stockage. C'est une expérience vivante.'; 'Huit parcours thématiques'). Add a CI lint failing if fr.json's accent density drops below a threshold (e.g. <1 accented char per 100 chars in any string >40 chars) so this regression class can never ship again.

title: Landing claims the family tree is "all integrated in your palace" — code shows zero tree-to-palace integration
detail: en.json:1161 (landing.features.familyTreeDesc): "...Then walk through the memories of each generation — all integrated in your palace." Verified: the entire family-tree module (src/app/(app)/family-tree/, 23 files) contains no reference to rooms, palace, or memory linking; the only 'memories' hit is PersonPanelPhoto.tsx:102-112 using the storage bucket for profile photos. No person→memory or person→room association exists anywhere. This is exactly the differentiator the comparison strategy leans on vs Ancestry/MyHeritage — an early adopter who tests it will feel misled.
section: Section 3, Enrich group — Family Tree card (en.json:1161, mirrored in nl/de/es/fr)
