It doesn't tell your story.'; I1 identity 'Become the keeper of your family's story.' Do NOT lead the main hero with mortality — reserve urgency for gift/adult-children surfaces.
section: Hero headline + subheadline (LandingClient.tsx:1140-1160; en.json landing.hero) + PostHog experiment
recommendation: Run a 4-arm PostHog experiment (already integrated): control vs O1 vs E2 vs I1, each with a rewritten sub of the shape [what it literally is] + [with whom] + [risk reversal]: "A beautiful 3D palace for your photos, voice recordings, and life stories — explore it together with your family. Free to start, no credit card needed." Primary metric = signup start; guardrail = tour-video clicks. Promote 'the questions your grandchildren would ask' to hero/sub-hero level. Also write one positioning sentence the visitor can repeat to a sibling: "The only place your family can walk through its memories together — and pass them on." Ship in all 5 locales; verify the iOS variant renders no paid copy.

title: The adult-child buyer and their urgency triggers are absent from all copy — every line addresses someone preserving their OWN story
detail: Every audience card, feature description, and CTA is first-person Keeper. The real triggers for the 38-45-year-old — a parent's diagnosis, the death of the first parent ('we never recorded dad'), dementia onset, milestone birthdays — appear nowhere; regret is the dominant emotion in the wild (viral Reddit/ScaryMommy threads are adult children listing what they wish they'd recorded). Remento's whole homepage is 'The most meaningful gift for parents'; StoryWorth's hero names the giver relationship in five words. 'Gift' appears exactly once in the entire landing namespace (an in-app string). The only urgency line ('Memories don't wait. Neither should you.') is generic and at the very bottom. Audience self-selection ('Who it's for') sits at position 9, behind the scroll trap.
section: Whole-page narrative (landing.hero, landing.audience, landing.cta) + audience section placement
recommendation: Add a second narrative track for the buyer-for-parent, in trigger order: (1) regret-prevention "One day you'll want to hear her voice again. Make sure you can."; (2) dignified urgency "Some stories can't wait for someday. Start with one question tonight."; (3) doer relief "You set it up in an evening. Dad just talks."; (4) gift "Better than flowers. Longer than a book." Move audience identification into the top third: a hero sub-device ('For your story — or as a gift for theirs') or a two-card split ('Build your own palace' / 'Give one to a parent'). Replace one audience card with one aimed at adult children.

title: No gift purchase flow — conceding the entire buying motion StoryWorth and Remento are built on, and the deadline-driven buyer has no way to pay
detail: Both competitors are gift-first (StoryWorth 'The gift of a lifetime', NYT Gift Guide; Remento's $99/yr gift with scheduled gift email and printable card) and their buyer is MP's exact secondary persona: the adult child purchasing at calendar moments (Mother's/Father's Day, Christmas, 70th/80th birthdays) or crisis moments (diagnosis). The repo has no gift capability: pricing/page.tsx handleSubscribe only supports self-serve checkout for the logged-in user; registration creates MY palace, not dad's. Every CTA says free, there's no pricing link in the visible flow, and 'free forever' even triggers 'what's the catch? how do they survive?' skepticism. Every seasonal search that converts on SW/RM is structurally unavailable.
recommendation: Ship a gift SKU (web only, sealed from iOS via mp_platform): Stripe checkout with recipient email + delivery date + personal message + printable gift-card PDF, priced as a year of Keeper (€99/yr — deliberately on the SW/RM anchor), redeemable via WhatsApp (which doubles as the zero-tech onboarding story). Build a /gift page anchored on "Give your parents a palace for their memories. A gift you build together" with "Record the stories while the storytellers can still tell them" and seasonal ad variants. Landing block: "The gift that doesn't end when the book ships."

title: Voice is the category-winning emotional asset — MP records, transcribes, and replays it in-room, but the page treats voice as a file type
detail: Remento's entire headline is 'A keepsake book that lets you hear their voice forever'; its top quote is about crying at a QR code of dad's voice. StoryWorth's most-cited weakness is being text-only. Grief and memory forums consistently rank voice as the most treasured artifact (people keep voicemails for years). MP genuinely has AI-guided voice interviews, WhatsApp voice notes, and in-room voice playback — arguably MORE powerful than voice-behind-a-QR — but on the page voice appears only inside 'AI-Guided Interviews' body text (en.json:1154-1155) and step-2 copy. Nothing at hero or section-header level says 'voice', and the page contains zero audio.
section: Feature grid (Capture group) + section 6 walkthrough + section headers
recommendation: Promote voice to its own headed moment: "Photos show what happened. Your voice tells why it mattered." / "Not a book they'll read once. A voice they can visit." In the walkthrough section: "Stand in her kitchen. Hear her tell the story in her own voice" — pair Guillaume's video with an audible voice-memory moment rather than silent screenshots.

title: Permanence and inheritance — the #1 trust answers for a legacy product — are buried in the unreachable FAQ and the ToS
detail: Two distinct fears, both answered in the repo but invisible: (1) 'What happens to the palace when I/he dies?' — forum/search research shows a large anxiety cluster (Google won't grant family access even with a death certificate; inactive accounts get deleted); MP's answer (Legacy Planning 'Choose who gets the keys', time capsules, comparison row4) sits in sections 8-9 below the trap, treated as feature card 12 of 12. (2) 'What if this company disappears?' — the repo contains a best-in-class answer: full ZIP export on the FREE tier (plans.ts:47), a contractual 90-day shutdown notice + export guarantee (ToS, en.json:3832), and FAQ q12 written exactly for this (en.json:1359-1360) — all invisible on a Terms page and a trapped FAQ. StoryWorth's structural advantage is a physical book that survives the company; MP's endgame is a 3D world behind a login with these questions unanswered. For the primary persona this is the reason to buy; for gift-givers, the reason to gift.
section: Legacy card + FAQ q6/q12 (LandingClient.tsx:2139; en.json:1346-1361) + missing trust section
recommendation: Two visible moments: (1) elevate legacy to the top third as named fear + resolution — "When a Google account goes quiet, the photos vanish with it. A palace has heirs." — with a second beat near the final CTA reusing 'Choose who gets the keys'; only promise mechanics that verifiably exist. (2) A named 'Forever Promise' block near the final CTA: "Export everything as a ZIP anytime, on every plan — and if we ever shut down, you get 90 days and your complete archive." Link the words to the ToS clause for credibility. Consider roadmapping a printed 'Palace Book' export (photo-book + QR to walk the room) — it neutralizes the only rows where book services win (physical keepsake, gift object).

title: "Is AI reading my family's private photos?" — the page advertises AI prominently, creating the objection without answering it
detail: FAQ a9 (en.json:1354) already says the right things — AI is opt-in, uses Anthropic's Claude which does not train on user data, EU storage — but it renders below the scroll trap, while 'AI-Guided Interviews' and 'AI sorts thousands of photos' are advertised above the fold with no reassurance. The site's own blog even coaches readers to ask vendors the AI-training question. AI copy also uses engineering verbs ('transcribes, tags, and places', 'opt-in', vendor names) that read as alien and mildly threatening to an AI-anxious demographic.
recommendation: Add a one-line footnote to every AI feature card: "AI is opt-in and never trains on your memories." In the FAQ lead with "Nothing happens without your permission, and your memories are never used to train anything" before naming the vendor; frame AI as 'a gentle interviewer — it asks, you talk'. Verify the 'does not train' claim against current Anthropic commercial terms before shipping.

title: The effort objection ('I don't have time to organize 40 years of photos') has the perfect rebuttal already written — hidden at body-copy size in one of 12 uniform cards
detail: The classic killer objection for memory/legacy products. The rebuttal exists at en.json:1151: "AI sorts thousands of photos into the right rooms in minutes. What would take you months happens while you have coffee." — currently one of 12 identical beige cards. AI interviews (2 free) also answer 'I can't write my life story'.
recommendation: Promote to a full-width band with a before/after visual (camera-roll chaos → organized rooms). Headline: "You bring the photos. AI does the sorting." Sub: "What would take you months happens while you have coffee — and if writing isn't your thing, the AI interviewer asks, you just talk."

title: "My family won't actually use this / I'll be alone in my palace" — real rebuttals exist but are never framed as the answer
detail: The silent-network objection: the Keeper fears building for nobody; the adult child fears mom won't keep it up. Existing rebuttals are scattered: co-creation (en.json:1344), WhatsApp contribution (anyone can forward a photo — near-zero friction), Receive Shared Memories, visitor Explore mode. None is framed as an answer to 'will my family join?'.
section: Share feature group (section 3) + section 6 walkthrough video
recommendation: Reframe the Share group intro: "You don't have to do this alone — and your family doesn't need to learn anything. They tap your link to walk through, and add their own photos just by sending a WhatsApp message." Show a two-generation moment in the walkthrough video, not a solo tour.

title: Five different labels for the same /register action destroy message consistency and fragment analytics
detail: The identical action carries five labels: nav 'Get Started' (LandingClient.tsx:941), hero + sticky 'Create Your Palace — Free' (1197, 2618), mid-page 'Store Your Memories Now' (1571), final 'Start Your Palace — Free' (2283), footer 'Get Started Free' (2429). NN/g senior-UX guidance: the same action must always carry the same literal label — each new label forces re-evaluation of whether this is a new commitment. 'Store Your Memories Now' is worst: it reframes the product as storage, the exact 'folder/passive drive' framing the hero and comparison table attack, and duplicates the how-it-works step-1 title. nl.json:1369 ('Maak je Palace — Gratis', untranslated vs hero 'Maak je Paleis') proves 5 labels x 5 locales = 25 independently drifting strings.
section: All CTAs (nav, hero, mid, final, footer, sticky, exit-intent) x 5 locales
recommendation: One primary label everywhere: "Create Your Palace" — brand-owned, outcome-explicit, and already what iOS shows after dash-stripping, so web and iOS become one string and the Apple seal is satisfied by construction. Web-only microcopy under the button: "Free forever · No credit card needed" (hidden when isIosApp); iOS microcopy: "Ready in minutes · No tech skills needed". Nav/footer: "Get Started". Never use "Store" in a CTA; rename step 1 to "Add Your Memories". Reference ONE message key (landing.cta.primary) from every render site. Locales: NL "Maak je Paleis", DE "Erstelle deinen Palast", ES "Crea tu palacio", FR "Créez votre palais".

title: CTA cadence and hierarchy broken: risk-reversal missing at the hero, secondary button equals the primary, no CTA across the longest stretch, mobile sticky is a ghost button, and the mini-CTA closes before any proof
detail: 'No tech skills needed' — arguably the #1 objection for 60+ — appears only in the unreachable final section; hero risk-reversal is crammed into the button label while chips answer security, not cost/difficulty. heroCta and heroSecondary (LandingClient.tsx:2751-2776) share identical padding/size/radius — only fill vs 1.5px 50%-alpha outline differs (a border that nearly vanishes on the dark video, failing 3:1 non-text contrast); on mobile both stack full-width, splitting the thumb's choice. Between hero and mid-CTA sit several viewports with zero conversion opportunity; no sticky exists on desktop, and the mobile-only sticky bar (2601-2619) renders its button transparent with a 60%-opacity border — the lowest-affordance treatment in the system, on the highest-persistence element. The mid-CTA itself ('no catch') fires before the visitor has seen video, screenshot, or testimonial — the close before the proof.
recommendation: Microcopy line under the hero primary: 'Free forever · No credit card · No tech skills needed' (AA contrast, i18n'd, iOS-gated). Demote the hero secondary to a text link with play icon ('▶ Watch the 90-second tour') at ~60% visual mass; make the primary the single unmissable element at first paint. Invert the sticky bar: near-solid bar, button in full darkened-gradient fill + shadow; keep footerInView hide logic and safe-area padding. Add one quiet inline CTA after the feature wall; downgrade the mid-CTA to a low-commitment ask ('Watch the tour') until proof has been presented; reserve 'no catch'-class reassurance for the final close.

title: "Watch How It Works" doesn't play anything — it scrolls to a text section while the demo video sits two sections lower (and below the trap)
detail: The hero secondary button (en.json:1123) promises video but its onClick (LandingClient.tsx:1199-1202) scrolls to #how-it-works — the three-step TEXT section (1435) — while the walkthrough lives in #showcase (1578), which nothing on the page links to. For older users a label→action mismatch is a direct trust hit at the most fragile moment (first interaction), and it squanders the page's best conversion asset: for a 3D product, the demo video IS the argument, and no CTA reliably reaches it. scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth'}) (1201) also ignores reduced motion. It's currently unmeasurable as a video CTA.
recommendation: Relabel to "Watch the 90-Second Tour" (specific duration lowers commitment anxiety) and open the walkthrough in a lightbox directly from the hero — no scroll dependency, immune to the carousel, identical on iOS (a video CTA carries no pricing; the click gesture grants autoplay-with-sound). Keep a small 'How it works' nav link for the text steps. Instrument play-rate and completion in PostHog.

title: Exit-intent modal: dark-pattern-adjacent for this audience, and a11y-broken (no dialog semantics, no Escape, no focus management, tiny close target)
detail: The overlay fires on mouseleave after 5 s (LandingClient.tsx:593-605, 2624-2717) with no role='dialog', no aria-modal, no aria-labelledby, no Escape handler, no focus trap; focus never moves in — screen-reader and keyboard users may not perceive it while it visually blocks the page (WCAG 4.1.2/2.4.3). The ✕ is a ~1.25rem glyph at 0.6 opacity with minimal padding — under the 24px WCAG 2.5.8 minimum, let alone the 44px seniors need. Combined with the scroll trap, the realistic journey is: scroll gets stuck, user moves to leave, modal pops up — for 60+ Heritage Keepers being asked to entrust their life's memories, an ambush at the exit contradicts the page's own 'no catch' promise. StoryWorth, Ancestry, and AARP don't use exit-intent modals. It also bypasses the iOS seal (covered separately).
recommendation: Preferred: remove the pattern entirely — once the trap is fixed, the final CTA and FAQ do the retention work; the ceiling is a small non-modal inline banner. If kept: role='dialog' aria-modal aria-labelledby, focus moved in and trapped, Escape closes, focus restored on close, 44x44px full-opacity close target, and the isIosApp gate.

title: prefers-reduced-motion and Save-Data are ignored page-wide — and HeroVideo actively fights the browser to force playback
detail: Grep finds no prefers-reduced-motion, saveData, or effectiveType checks in LandingClient.tsx. The hero video autoplays, loops indefinitely with no pause control (WCAG 2.2.2 failure), and if autoplay is blocked attaches document-wide click/touchstart listeners to force .play() on the user's first interaction anywhere (107-131) — actively defeating the user agent's data/battery protections. globals.css:361 zeroes CSS animations under reduced-motion but does nothing for <video>, ScrollFadeIn's JS-driven states, the sticky-CTA slide, or JS smooth scroll. Vestibular sensitivity rises sharply with age — an unstoppable full-viewport motion loop behind the headline hits exactly the 60+ target, on older iPads paying continuous GPU cost.
recommendation: Gate on matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'): show the poster and never call play() (delete the forced-play listeners in that branch), render ScrollFadeIn final state immediately, suppress sticky/exit transitions, use scrollIntoView behavior:'auto'. Skip video download on navigator.connection.saveData or 2g/3g. Add a visible pause button. Table stakes for a seniors-focused product — and the static branch also fixes the brown-void first paint.

title: Structured data: fabricated aggregateRating (4.8 from 12), duplicate conflicting Organization graphs, 404 logo, empty sameAs, dead Play badge feeding JSON-LD
detail: layout.tsx:216-246 hard-codes aggregateRating 4.8 / ratingCount 12 on WebApplication with no reviews visible anywhere (testimonials are lazy-gated below the trap) — self-serving review markup unsupported by visible content, a documented trigger for structured-data manual actions that would strip ALL rich results. Two competing ld+json graphs: layout.tsx (logo /brand/alt-social-512.png, exists) vs LandingClient.tsx:624-679 (second Organization pointing at https://thememorypalace.ai/logo.png — public/logo.* does not exist, 404s; sameAs is literally []). The FAQPage block (646) ships a2's 'bank-grade/highest security standards' puffery into Google answer boxes, and FAQ a8 claims 'Download it from the App Store or Google Play' while the rendered Play badge URL is literally '#' (en.json:1364, used at 2194) — a dead store badge is exactly the detail a cautious gift-giver clicks to vet legitimacy. FAQ rich results have also been restricted to gov/health sites since 2023.
recommendation: Merge into ONE server-rendered @graph: Organization (one existing logo URL, populated sameAs), WebSite, WebApplication + free Offer, VideoObject. Delete aggregateRating until real, visible, verifiable on-page reviews exist — then generate it from the same data the testimonials render. Point playStoreUrl at the real Play listing (one exists per memory notes) or remove the badge and soften a8. Audit every FAQ answer feeding the schema for claims you'd accept quoted verbatim in a Google snippet.

title: Head metadata is keyword-empty and technically broken: bare title, 5-word description, no canonical/metadataBase, 512x512 OG logo, no sitemap/robots for 28+ blog posts
detail: src/app/layout.tsx:30-67: default title is just 'The Memory Palace' and the site-wide description 'Your memories, given a home.' is duplicated into OG/Twitter — no category term (digital memory book, family legacy app, 3D photo album), no benefit, no CTA in the SERP snippet. No metadataBase (relative OG URLs may resolve to the Vercel deployment domain) and zero 'canonical' anywhere in src/app, so every ?lang=/tracking variant is a potential duplicate. og:image is a 512x512 logo while twitter card is summary_large_image (expects ~1200x630) — shares look like an icon, not a product — though an ImageResponse route already exists (api/og/route.tsx). Audits conflict on whether app/sitemap.ts exists (one found none plus no robots; another found lastModified stamped new Date() at build) — verify on the current branch; either way the ~28-slug x 5-locale blog is unadvertised and unlinked from the landing.
recommendation: Rewrite keyword-led: title 'The Memory Palace — Your Family's Memories in a 3D Home You Can Walk Through' (also mitigates the podcast name collision); description 'The ancient memory-palace technique, rebuilt in 3D — preserve photos, voices and life stories in rooms you can walk through. Free, EU-hosted, GDPR.' Add metadataBase: new URL('https://thememorypalace.ai') + alternates.canonical '/'. Build a 1200x630 branded OG image showing the actual 3D villa interior. Verify/add app/sitemap.ts (homepage, /pricing, /security, /help, all blog slugs per locale) with real content dates and app/robots.ts; add a footer block linking 3-5 cornerstone blog posts.

title: hreflang points 5 locales at ?lang= URLs that all serve identical English HTML — 11,250 translated keys earning zero EU rankings
detail: layout.tsx:68-76 declares alternates.languages as https://thememorypalace.ai?lang=nl|de|es|fr, but locale comes from a client-side cookie (mp_locale via useTranslation), so the server renders English regardless of the query param. Google validates hreflang by fetching each URL; finding identical content it discards the cluster. Full NL/DE/ES/FR landing copy earns nothing in exactly the EU markets (NL/BE, DACH) where a GDPR/EU-hosted family product should dominate. No x-default; the sitemap omits the variants.
recommendation: Move locales to SSR path segments (/nl, /de, /es, /fr) that render translated HTML server-side, emit reciprocal hreflang + x-default on every variant, and translate title/description per locale. Dutch queries like 'digitaal herinneringsboek' and 'familiegeschiedenis app' are low-competition wins. If path-based locales are out of scope for this release, drop the hreflang block entirely rather than ship an invalid cluster.

title: H1 and every H2 are poetic but carry zero query language — the page can only rank for its brand name
detail: The H1 'Your memories deserve a palace, not a folder' and H2s ('Twelve ways your memories stay vivid.', 'Three steps. Five minutes.', 'Your palace, from the inside', 'THIS IS NOT A PHOTO ALBUM.') contain not one searched term (digital memory book, family legacy app, online memory palace, preserve family memories, 3D photo album). The page's only keyword-bearing sentence is buried in FAQ answer a1. Emotional headlines are right for conversion, but with no keyword-bearing support structure the page competes for nothing — compounded by the podcast name collision on the bare brand term.
recommendation: Keep the emotional H1; make the support do SEO work: a keyword-rich subhead under the hero ('The 3D digital memory book for family stories, photos and voices') and H2s pairing emotion with category terms ('A family legacy app in three steps', 'Your online memory palace, from the inside'). Give the hero eyebrow descriptive text since it visually precedes the H1.

title: One monolithic page traps 14+ distinct search intents — feature cards and the comparison table are unexploited ranking pages
detail: All intent — WhatsApp capture, family tree, time capsules, legacy planning, memory map, AI interviews — is trapped as small non-linking cards inside one client component. Each maps to a distinct query ('family tree app with photos', 'digital time capsule for family', 'AI life story interview') a single page can never rank for simultaneously. The comparison table is exactly the bottom-funnel content that ranks as '[competitor] alternative' pages — currently below the scroll trap and invisible to crawlers via LazySection. The landing also never links to /explore (the only social-proof surface) or any /kep marketing page (the public one built 2026-05-13 no longer exists — /kep now redirects to the authed app).
section: Information architecture / content strategy + footer/nav links
recommendation: Build /features/[slug] pages (hero shot, 3 benefits, screenshot, FAQ, CTA — the mega-menu pattern already planned for STEMMA is the right model) and link each landing card to its page. Add /compare/google-photos and /compare/apple-photos reusing existing table copy. Add /explore to nav or footer; decide whether a public /kep marketing page should exist again. This de-bloats the landing and creates 14+ indexable, conversion-ready URLs.

title: The page has three competing personalities — heritage hotel, fintech vault, growth-hacker SaaS — plus fear-based closers; commit to one voice charter
detail: en.json's landing copy oscillates between (a) heritage-hotel brochure ('Cinematic 3D Palace', 'marble footsteps echo'), (b) fintech vault ('256-bit Bank-Grade Encryption'), and (c) growth-hacker SaaS ('Like Duolingo — but for the stories that matter most', 'drag, drop, done', 'No credit card, no catch'). A 68-year-old meets a concierge, a bank teller, and an app marketer on one page — nothing is memorable. The closers use the wrong levers: 'Memories don't wait. Neither should you.' is mortality pressure aimed at a 72-year-old (fear, not love), and 'THIS IS NOT A PHOTO ALBUM.' all-caps shouts and defines the brand by what it isn't.
section: Whole page copy (en.json landing.*) + final CTA + carousel header
recommendation: Commit to ONE personality — the Loving Archivist: second person, concrete family nouns (kitchen table, wedding day, your mother's voice), unhurried verbs (keep, place, seal, hand over), zero urgency, zero app-jargon. Write a 5-line voice charter (say/never-say: no all-caps, no deadlines, no competitor names, no 'don't') and rewrite every landing.* key against it. Closers become invitations: 'Begin with one memory. The rest will follow.' Carousel header: 'Step inside. This is what a memory looks like when it has a home.' Test: cover the logo — if the copy could belong to Dropbox or a bank, rewrite.

title: Insider jargon throughout: 'wings' undefined, 'GEDCOM', 'pedigree' x3, 'streaks/badges/Like Duolingo', AI engineering verbs — hostile to the 60+ reader and tonally wrong beside grief content
detail: (1) 'wings' first appears undefined in card 2 and is load-bearing in the free-plan FAQ; (2) 'GEDCOM import' (comparison row 6, FAQ a7) is a 1984 file-format acronym only hobbyists know; (3) 'fan charts, pedigree views, relationship links' repeats verbatim in three places — 'pedigree' reads as dog-breeding to lay readers; (4) memoryTracksDesc sells via gamification culture ('Earn badges, build streaks… Like Duolingo', en.json:1163, echoed at 1218/1223 and comparison row8) — naming another app breaks the spell, gamification vocabulary trivializes sacred life-story work adjacent to testimonials about a dead husband and dementia, and it simultaneously signals recall-training to memory-technique enthusiasts when it's actually autobiography prompts (a bait-and-switch for that persona); (5) AI copy uses engineering verbs ('transcribes, tags, and places', 'opt-in', vendor names).
section: Sections 3, 6, 8 + FAQ (en.json landing.features, landing.comparison, faq) — 5 locales
recommendation: Translate every term into outcomes: 'share a room or a whole chapter of your palace (like Childhood or Travels)'; 'Bring in the family tree you already built on Ancestry or MyHeritage — no retyping' (GEDCOM in parentheses in one FAQ line only); 'See five generations at a glance' with the fan chart SHOWN, not named; Journeys card → 'One gentle question at a time, your life story takes shape. Start with your childhood street; end with the wisdom you want to pass on' — never 'streaks', never a competitor's name (keep achievements inside the app); 'You talk; your words are written down for you.' Adopt the researched vocabulary map as the copy style guide: USE 'life story', 'in your own words', 'keepsake', 'pass down', 'grandchildren', 'shoebox/attic', 'no tech skills needed', 'yours forever'; DROP 'folder', 'gamified', 'cinematic flyover', coined persona titles.

title: The page never pays off its own name — the 2,500-year method-of-loci story is the uncopyable differentiator, already written in 5 locales, and completely absent
detail: Grep confirms zero mentions of loci/mnemonic/Simonides/spatial memory in LandingClient.tsx or landing.* copy, yet a full 5-locale blog post exists (slug what-is-memory-palace-technique, src/lib/blog/posts/en.ts:8), linked from nowhere. The story is uniquely defensible (book services and photo-storage products cannot claim it), backed by citable science (Krokos, Plaisant & Varshney 2018: immersive virtual memory palaces improved recall 8.8% vs desktop), and matches the Tuscan aesthetic. It is also the missing argument behind 'THIS IS NOT A PHOTO ALBUM' — currently assertion without argument — and the answer to 'is 3D a gimmick?'. FAQ a1 (emitted as JSON-LD) defines 'memory palace' purely as a 3D keepsake space, guaranteeing SERP intent mismatch for the site's most rankable query; technique enthusiasts landing via 'memory palace app' find no hook and read the name as term-squatting. Guardrail: copy must describe spatial memory as why the PRODUCT's organization works, never as user-cognition benefit — 'improves your memory' / dementia framing would be an unsubstantiated therapeutic claim under EU consumer-protection rules.
section: New 'Why a palace?' band between hero and features + FAQ a1/q0 + JSON-LD (LandingClient.tsx:646) + blog link
recommendation: Add a short supporting band — "Why a palace? Because your brain thinks in places." Body: "For 2,500 years — from Simonides to Cicero's Rome — people remembered what mattered by placing it in imagined rooms. Scientists call it the method of loci: we recall places far better than files. (Prefer a simple list? The Library shows everything as a classic gallery too.)" CTA: "Read the 2,500-year story →" to the existing blog post. Add FAQ q0 'What is a memory palace?' (technique-first answer, mirrored in JSON-LD, all 5 locales). Approved phrases: 'your brain remembers places better than files', 'the same principle used by memory champions'. Banned: 'improves memory', 'trains your brain', anything touching aging/dementia. Clarifier for enthusiasts: 'We use the palace to keep memories, not to train them.'

title: Name collision: 'The Memory Palace' is culturally owned by a Peabody-finalist podcast, a 2024 Random House book, and the generic technique — qualify everywhere, don't rename
detail: Nate DiMeo's podcast (since 2008, Radiotopia/PRX) holds thememorypalace.us AND .org; Random House published a companion book Nov 2024. The bare term is dominated in search by technique explainers, Sherlock, and 'Moonwalking with Einstein'. layout.tsx metadata titles are just 'The Memory Palace' with a 5-word tagline — indistinguishable from the podcast in a SERP snippet. A discoverability tax and weak positioning, not a rename-level problem (different class: entertainment vs software).
recommendation: Qualify everywhere: title tag → 'The Memory Palace — Your Family's Memories in a 3D Home You Can Walk Through' (+ locale equivalents). Add alternateName ["Memory Palace app", "family memory palace"] and applicationCategory to the SoftwareApplication JSON-LD. Target long-tail the podcast can't hold ('memory palace app for family memories') via the definition block + existing blog post. Optional hygiene: EUIPO/USPTO clearance check for software/SaaS classes before further brand investment.

title: German addresses 60+ buyers as 'du' with literal calques no native copywriter would write
detail: de.json uses informal 'du' throughout ('Erstelle deinen Palast'). German Heritage Keepers 60+ overwhelmingly expect 'Sie' from a product simultaneously selling DSGVO compliance and legacy planning — 'du' from a stranger reads presumptuous to this cohort (unlike NL 'je'). The final CTA compounds it with a word-for-word calque: 'Erinnerungen warten nicht. Du solltest es auch nicht.' — grammatically odd German. Ancestry.de and MyHeritage.de use Sie.
section: All DE sections, esp. final CTA (src/messages/de.json landing.cta.title, landing.hero)
recommendation: Make a deliberate, documented register decision per market; for the DE 60+ heritage segment Siezen is the safe default. Rewrite calqued lines natively ('Erinnerungen warten nicht. Warten Sie auch nicht.'). Run a native DE review pass of the full landing namespace either way.

title: Locales are stale vintages of old English copy with no source-of-truth process — the same key tells a different product story per language
detail: features.sharingDesc: EN says 'Your best friend adds that holiday video from 1998'; NL/DE/FR all say your brother and append sentences EN doesn't have; ES reorders and invents content. hero.description: all four locales dropped 'friends', contradicting the co-creation positioning. hero.headline: EN was rewritten but NL/DE/ES/FR still translate the previous version. Remaining polish: NL keeps gamer anglicisms ('bouw streaks op', 'Verdien badges') and English Title Case ('Maak je Paleis — Gratis'); ES cta.title dangles ('Tú tampoco deberías.'); DE/FR strings run 30-50% longer than EN while navLink uses whiteSpace:'nowrap' + flexShrink:0 (LandingClient.tsx:2735-2736) — the nav will collide at tablet widths in FR/DE — and the hero's hard line-break is tuned for the 31-char EN first line vs DE's 42.
recommendation: Treat EN as master and re-translate every landing key from current EN in one sweep (native register per market: NL 'in je eigen woorden', sentence case; ES 'No esperes tú tampoco'). Then enforce sync: a script that diffs key sets and flags keys whose EN value changed after the locale file's last edit (key-versioning or a lightweight TMS). QA the landing at 768-1200px in DE/FR; shorten nav labels per locale (DE 'Ablauf', FR 'Fonctions') and give translators explicit length budgets. Document the tú/vous/Sie/je register decision per market.

title:
Hero headline widow is engineered in: hard
plus a max-width the clamped size can't honor — guaranteed broken in DE/NL
detail:
LandingClient.tsx:1123-1145 renders the H1 as {storyDeserves}
{moreThanFolder} at clamp(2.5rem, 6.5vw, 4.75rem) with maxWidth 53.125rem. At 1440px the size resolves to 76px; the 31-char first line can't fit 850px at 76px Cormorant, so it wraps naturally BEFORE the manual break — producing the observed orphan 'palace,' alone on its own line, comma dangling. In DE ('Deine Erinnerungen verdienen einen Palast,' — 42 chars) the widow is guaranteed. A hard
inside a fluid-width, fluid-size, 5-locale headline assumes a line length the layout never guarantees — it breaks the rhythm of the page's single most important sentence and reads like a typo to a careful older reader.
recommendation:
Remove the
; add textWrap:'balance' (evergreen support, harmless fallback) and keep the semantic break by binding 'a palace,' with whiteSpace:'nowrap' or restructuring so the gold italic phrase is the natural second line — enemy and promise on the same visual line. Widen maxWidth to ~60rem or cap the clamp at ~4.25rem so the first line fits at 1440px in every locale. Treat headline wrap points as locale-tested, never hard-coded; verify at 1280/1440/1920.

title: Display typography too frail and font loading too heavy: Cormorant 300 hero over video, Cormorant below its optical floor at card size, 14 WOFF2 files with display:swap FOUT in the LCP element
detail: The H1 (LandingClient.tsx:1128) and every sectionTitle (2792) use Cormorant Garamond at weight 300 — a high-contrast, low-x-height face whose hairlines shimmer against the dark video, which is why the hero needs two stacked text-shadows (1137) as a crutch; the gold italic accent line (1142) is the lowest-legibility combination available (italic + light + serif over motion). featureTitle runs Cormorant at 21px (2807-2813) — below the ~24px floor where the face stays crisp. Meanwhile layout.tsx:15-28 loads Cormorant in 5 weights x 2 styles + Manrope in 4 weights (14 WOFF2, ~150-200 KB largely unused) with display:'swap' — Cormorant is metrically very different from Georgia, so the swap visibly re-shapes the LCP headline; a redundant fonts.googleapis preconnect (line 250) remains though next/font self-hosts. No element uses text-wrap balance/pretty, so every heading in 5 locales is one resize from a widow.
section: Hero + section titles + card titles + src/app/layout.tsx:15-28, 250
recommendation: Move display type to weight 500 (already loaded), 600 for the gold italic; remove the second text-shadow once weight carries contrast. Reserve Cormorant for ≥1.75rem; set card titles in Manrope 600 at 1.0625-1.125rem. Trim the load to ~4-5 files (Cormorant 400/500 + one italic, Manrope 400/600); remove the preconnect; verify adjustFontFallback produces shift-free swaps. Add textWrap:'balance' to h1/h2/h3 and 'pretty' to paragraphs page-wide — directly hardens the DE/FR/NL locales where strings run 15-30% longer.

title: T.font family strings don't match next/font-loaded fonts — inline styles likely render Georgia/system instead of the brand faces
detail: next/font/google with `variable` registers fonts under hashed internal family names exposed only through --font-display/--font-body (set on <html>, layout.tsx:104). But T.font.display is the literal "'Cormorant Garamond', Georgia, serif", there is no Google Fonts stylesheet <link> (only preconnects) and no @font-face CSS — so inline styles using F.display/F.body likely render Georgia/system fonts. The overhaul branch already fixes this pattern ("var(--font-display), ...").
recommendation: Change T.font.* to reference var(--font-display)/var(--font-body) with fallbacks (mirror the overhaul branch), and verify in-browser which family actually renders before any typography decisions are made on top of it.

title: Warm-dark design system (HUD/motion/gradient tokens) is stranded on the overhaul/design-perf branch — the redesign has no tokens to build on
detail: The intended candlelight HUD tokens (T.hud, T.motion, T.gradient, T.archive), the muted-color WCAG fix, and the Playfair/Inter/JetBrains font system exist only on overhaul/design-perf; staging has none of them. Meanwhile LandingClient.tsx uses only T.color/T.font and hand-rolls everything else — ~15 raw hex literals (e.g. #1a1a18, #3D3D3A dark-section gradients) bypass the palette, which explains the beige-on-beige inconsistency and makes any re-theme require touching every inline style.
recommendation: Cherry-pick or port the theme.ts token additions (ADD-only per the file's own comment) to staging before redesigning, and decide whether the redesign uses the hud (candlelight amber) or archive (oxblood/museum) accent language — they are two different systems. Route dark-section backgrounds and muted text through tokens; adopt T.space/fontSize/radius during the redesign.

title: SSR HTML is desktop layout on phones (hydration flash), and the sticky CTA reads window.innerHeight during render
detail: All three responsive JS hooks return false during SSR, so every inline-style ternary renders the desktop value in server HTML. Only the nav is guarded (mounted state, LandingClient.tsx:402-403) and only hero title/subtitle have CSS !important overrides — stats grid, feature grids, comparison table, and footer paint desktop-sized on a phone until hydration. Two overlapping breakpoint systems coexist (JS hooks at 479/767/1024 vs CSS queries at 480/640/768). Related: showStickyBottomCta (line 590) computes visibility from window.innerHeight inline during render — non-reactive to resize/orientation and a render-time browser-global read.
section: Whole page responsive architecture + sticky CTA (LandingClient.tsx:402-403, 590)
recommendation: Prefer CSS-first responsiveness in the redesign (media queries / clamp / auto-fit grids) with one consolidated breakpoint set shared between any remaining hooks and CSS. Derive the sticky-CTA threshold in the scroll effect or a resize-aware hook.

title: Whole 2,719-line page re-renders on every scroll frame via setScrollY
detail: LandingClient.tsx:575-581 attach a scroll listener calling setScrollY(el.scrollTop) unthrottled, and scrollY is state on the component rendering the entire page — on mobile CPUs the full tree (12 cards, 8 comparison rows, footer, all inline-style objects re-allocated) reconciles up to 60-120x/second during scroll. The state feeds only three threshold booleans: headerOpaque (>60), scroll-hint fade (>50), sticky CTA (>innerHeight). A primary cause of scroll jank on mid-range Android — exactly the devices Heritage Keepers' families own.
recommendation: Replace numeric scrollY state with threshold booleans that only setState when they flip, or isolate nav/hint/sticky-CTA into tiny components fed by IntersectionObserver sentinels. Zero re-renders of the page body during scroll is the baseline; the redesign's component split should make this structural.

title: No shared marketing header/footer — nav duplicated with divergent links across 4+ pages, and the header omits the strongest scent anchors
detail: LandingClient, /pricing (L164-225), /blog (L66-134), /security (L322-397) each hand-roll their own header and footer with divergent link sets (blog header lacks /pricing; security footer only has /privacy + /terms) — a landing redesign that restyles nav will leave subpages inconsistent unless each is edited separately. The landing header itself (871-941) offers Features/How It Works/Pricing/Blog/Sign In/Get Started but omits the three things 60+ buyers and their gift-giving children scan for: FAQ (only discoverable by scrolling past the trap), the demo video (#showcase has an id but zero inbound links), and /security (footer + one small hero link only).
recommendation: Extract shared MarketingHeader/MarketingFooter into src/components/landing/ during the redesign and adopt them on all four pages. Add 'FAQ' (anchor) and 'See it in action' (#showcase/lightbox) to the header; keep Pricing but let the landing preview the free tier.

title: The page never shows what happens after clicking Get Started — no screenshots in how-it-works, no desktop view of the 3D product
detail: The 3-step section renders only a number, title, and one-line description per step (LandingClient.tsx:1472-1529) — zero screenshots of registration, onboarding, or the first-palace flow. The only product visuals on the page are one 16:9 video and eight portrait phone screenshots inside the trapped carousel; the desktop 3D experience — the product's core — is never shown as a desktop screenshot. For anxious 60+ Heritage Keepers, 'what will it ask me to do?' has no visual answer.
recommendation: Pair each step with a real annotated screenshot or 5-second clip of that exact moment (sign-up form, first room, first memory placed), Airbnb/Duolingo style. Add at least one large desktop screenshot of the 3D palace above the fold or in features. Reuse existing FAQ answers ('free forever', 'no credit card' — web only) as microcopy under the step imagery.

title: No human being or legal entity stands behind the product anywhere — anonymous footer is disqualifying for an heirloom product and an Impressum problem in DE
detail: Footer copyright is just 'The Memory Palace' (en.json:1309) — no legal entity, no address, no About page, no founder name or face, no contact email (only /help), no social links (Organization JSON-LD ships sameAs: []). FAQ a10's honest 'small, independent European team' answer is buried below the scroll trap. For a product asking families to deposit irreplaceable memories, anonymity is disqualifying — and for DE-market visitors an Impressum is legally required despite the DE locale being offered. App-store badges are buried in the FAQ section instead of the footer.
recommendation: Add a founder block — name, photo, two sentences on why you built this (ideally your own family's palace) — linked from the landing and footer ('Built by [name] in [city]'). Add legal entity + registered address + contact email to the footer, an /about or /imprint page, social profiles + populated sameAs, and app-store badges in the footer. StoryWorth, Remento, and Permanent.org all lead with founders because heirloom products are bought on the credibility of the humans promising to keep the lights on.

title: Landing shows zero pricing — subscription-fatigued visitors read absent pricing as hidden pricing, and the paper math vs book-included competitors goes unanswered
detail: The current web landing has no pricing section (only 'Free Forever Plan' and 'no catch'). Verified facts worth showing: free = unlimited wings/rooms/memories + 1 GB (plans.ts:34-38); Keeper €9.99/mo annual or €12.99 monthly with 7-day trial (plans.ts:54-55, 75); Guardian €19.99/€24.99. The gift-giver runs the math: Keeper ≈ €120/yr with no physical artifact vs StoryWorth $59 INCLUDING a hardcover — the page must anchor free-first to win that comparison, and MP's free-forever tier is unique in the category. Any pricing block must never render for mp_platform=ios (the FAQ a4/a4_ios pattern is the template).
section: Section 5 micro-CTA area (web only, iOS-sealed) + pricing framing
recommendation: Add a compact 3-tier pricing strip on web only, anchored free-first: "Free forever — unlimited rooms, 1 GB of memories, full export. Upgrade from €9.99/month only when you outgrow the space. Cancel anytime." Reuse the a4_ios gating pattern so iOS shows nothing. Surface "trial auto-cancels, never auto-charges" (verified: payment_method_collection 'if_required' + missing_payment_method 'cancel', api/stripe/checkout/route.ts:115-125) — almost no competitor can say it.

title: No section rhythm: identical centered templates on two near-identical beiges with flat 6.25rem pauses, then ~14:1 dark cliffs — the 'dead whitespace' feel is systemic
detail: All light sections reuse the same sectionLabel + centered sectionTitle pattern (LandingClient.tsx:2778, 2789); backgrounds alternate only between linen #F2EDE4 and warmStone #E5DDD0 (1.15:1 apart) separated by 1px 20-30%-alpha hairlines; white cards sit at 1.12:1 on linen with 3-4%-alpha decorative tints that are literally imperceptible; comparison and final CTA are both linen back-to-back, merging into one long beige field. Desktop paddings are a flat 6.25rem for nearly every section while internal spacing uses 15+ ad-hoc values on no scale; connective bands (stats 3rem, micro-CTA 3.5rem) read as accidental compression. Then three charcoal sections arrive as abrupt ~14:1 cliffs (two adjacent, wasting one). Containers use seven different max-widths (68.75/68/62.5/56.25/53.125/43.75/37.5rem), so the text column wanders and no grid is established; heading proximity is inverted — the eyebrow+H2 lockup floats 3.5-4rem from its own content.
recommendation: Build a 4-step tonal scale (cream #FCFAF5 → linen → a true mid like sandstone → charcoal), sequence it so every boundary is ≥1.3:1 and dark blocks are approached via a mid step, used as intentional contrast anchors. Define a spacing scale in theme.ts and use nothing else: 8px-base ladder + three tokens (sectionY = clamp(5rem, 8vw, 7.5rem), bandY ~3rem, headingGap 3rem); bands share the background of the section above. Two container tokens only: containerWide 72rem and containerProse 42rem. Heading cluster: label → 0.75rem → H2 → 1rem → one-line intro → 3rem → content.

title: No enforced type scale: ~16 ad-hoc font sizes and 6+ line-heights while theme.ts tokens go unused
detail: theme.ts:52 defines a 7-step fontSize token scale, yet LandingClient.tsx hardcodes at least sixteen distinct sizes (0.625-2.25rem plus four different clamp() recipes at 686, 1127, 2250, 2791) and six-plus line-heights. Adjacent text levels differ by 1-2px steps the eye reads as sameness — feeding the weak-hierarchy feel — while the jump from 21px card title to 44px section title has no intermediate rhythm. letterSpacing is specified in px at five values on rem-sized text.
recommendation: Collapse to one modular scale (ratio ~1.2, base 1.125rem for this audience): micro 0.75 / body-s 1 / body 1.125 / lead 1.3125 / h4 1.5 / h3 1.875 / h2 clamp(2-3rem) / h1 clamp(2.75-4.5rem), each with a paired line-height token, sourced from theme.ts so landing and app stop drifting. Tokenize tracking in em (trackWide 0.18em eyebrows, trackMicro 0.08em). World-class marketing sites ship 7-9 text styles total.

title: Two weak video moments instead of one hero-grade cinematic film — the strongest asset the product owns is never seen clearly
detail: The video budget is split between an invisible 18 s ambience loop (hero, triple-dimmed) and a 12 MB silent screen-capture buried behind the scroll trap. Neither shows the emotional core — a family's real memories inside walkable 3D rooms — at hero-grade quality, despite the product having a genuinely cinematic 3D villa and an existing 5-waypoint exterior flyover (2026-04-18 session). public/video also ships ~16 MB of dead variants (hero-bg-original.mp4 12.5 MB, hero-bg-slow 2.4 MB, hero-bg-fast 1.7 MB — zero references in src/) publicly fetchable with every deploy.
recommendation: Script a single 60 s cinematic product film: golden-hour exterior flyover → doors open → glide through 2-3 rooms with real photos/voice memories playing → grandchild and grandparent reaction → 'Your memories deserve a palace' end card. Use its best 10-15 s as the fully-visible hero loop and the full narrated cut in the click-to-play lightbox from both hero CTAs. Keep 'Guillaume's Palace' authenticity as social proof. Encode AV1/WebM + H.264, hero loop <1.5 MB, with posters. Move the unused masters out of public/ (keep hero-bg-original locally as the re-encode source).

title: Re-sequence the page as promise → show → proof → close, structured around three JTBD lanes — the current order argues category superiority before showing or proving anything
detail: The current arc is promise → 12-card feature catalog → text steps → close-before-proof, with everything emotional (testimonials, comparison, FAQ, final CTA) at positions 8-13 behind the trap. The 65-year-old's actual jobs: JOB 1 (emotional, dominant) 'Be known by my grandchildren, in my own voice, before it's too late'; JOB 2 (functional) 'Finally deal with the pile: shoeboxes, 4 devices, 50,000 unsorted photos'; JOB 3 (relational) 'Give or receive a meaningful gift that becomes a family project'. The page argues a fourth thing — superiority over Google Photos — which is the adult child's rational justification, not anyone's trigger. Each job has a different entry emotion (longing / relief / love).
recommendation: After the hero: three job lanes — (1) 'Be remembered' (voice + interviews + time capsules; keep 'Some words mean more when they arrive at the right moment'); (2) 'Bring order to a lifetime of photos' (cloud import + AI sorting); (3) 'Do it together' (co-creation + gift entry). Then product demonstration → proof (one full-bleed pull-quote from a REAL user directly after the hero once verified; testimonials after 'Three steps') → comparison as rational close → FAQ immediately before the final CTA. At least one trust element within the first two viewport-heights.

title: Final CTA is the visually weakest moment at the point of highest intent
detail: The closing section is plain linen with a palace illustration at opacity 0.04 (LandingClient.tsx:2222-2244) — effectively invisible — immediately after another linen section, so the page ends in an undifferentiated beige whisper before the dark footer. A visitor who made it through the whole narrative gets no visual climax; the last impression is the flattest screen on the page.
recommendation: End on a peak: reuse the hero villa imagery properly bright, or a warm golden-hour palace render as full-bleed background; scale the headline to hero size and make the (darkened rustDeep) CTA the single highest-contrast element on the screen.

title: Gold brand accent is unusable on 70% of the page, splitting the site into two disconnected palettes
detail: Gold #D4AF37 appears three times and performs beautifully on charcoal (8.1:1) — but measures 1.8:1 on linen (goldDark only 2.5:1), so the signature accent that defines the brand in the hero vanishes for every light section, where the accent role silently switches to (failing) terracotta. Gold-on-dark luxury up top; orange-on-beige utility below.
recommendation: Codify a two-mode accent in theme.ts: gold = dark-background text accent + light-background graphic-only accent (rules, icon strokes, 2px card top-borders — non-text needs only 3:1); rustDeep #9A4F2A = light-background text accent. Thread gold as a graphic element through light sections (e.g. make the divider rules at 1721/1933 gold) so the hero's luxury cue persists down-page.
